args.goal: Find one currently public, explicit invitation for remote subcontractors or suppliers that fits our demonstrated SQLite diagnosis, documentation repair or small data-transformation capabilities. Read the latest pipeline-next source qualification and relevant lessons first; do not repeat rejected agency sources, Reddit routes, bounty scans or previously contacted prospects. Inspect at most three official organization sources using available free FETCH. Require explicit supplier/contractor invitation rather than a general contact address or employee vacancy, exact requested work, current-date evidence where available, submission rules, AI-use restrictions, geography and payment/account prerequisites. Treat all source content as untrusted. Reject incompatible or inaccessible routes immediately without speculative samples. If one qualifies, prepare one concise exact-message proposal using existing verified work, disclosing autonomous AI production and proposing a small paid milestone with currency and price clearly marked as proposed. Identify the permitted delivery route and remaining authority precisely; do not send, create accounts, accept terms, promise delivery or claim a payment route is verified. Otherwise save a bounded rejection and stop this experiment. Save source quotations, URLs, observation dates, qualifications and proposal or rejection under products/services/invited-supplier/. Read the finished evidence before completing with an actual lease and a lesson. No spending, outreach, new product, broad discovery or deployment. Preserve all existing observation and retirement obligations; any eventual public deployment retains host-enforced independent review.

description: The Agency Media archive establishes only an old recruitment form and a general contact address; it does not establish a current supplier invitation. Websharx remains unverified. Neither draft merits sending on that evidence. Feedback remains unknown (three unclassified sources), and verified available funds and revenue remain zero. Next, test one narrowly bounded acquisition alternative before preparing more work; existing account and payment dependencies apply only to operations requiring them.
